warnings: Unlike หน้า15, the mark choice here does not follow a strict horizontal/vertical rule — both B1 and B2 are used for horizontal AND vertical segments depending on position (verified on 2x-2.3x zoom crops of every segment except the one flagged below). B4 is used only for the two beams flanking the stairwell void's upper (A-B) portion; B2 is used for the same void's lower (B-C) portion. All beams on this sheet are at level +3.65 except the stair-landing support beam at grid2-3/row C (+2.10, matching หน้า15's ground-floor equivalent exactly).

CORRECTED 2026-08-24 (Makham, y-axis dummy rows — see grid master warnings). The beam previously recorded as 'B1 A2-A3 (+3.65)' does not exist: a pixel scan of the grid2-grid3 band at row A (y=768 px) finds only the thin dash-dot grid line (c≈130), not a beam double-line, whereas the same row in grid1-2 and grid3-4 shows clear beam face pairs at y=758/779. The upper stair void's two real edge beams sit on the new dummy rows A' (-1.10, faces at y=652/673) and A'' (+0.80, faces at y=852/873) — the void straddles row A rather than starting at it. Both are now recorded separately, and the S1 grid_ref was updated to match.

RESOLVED 2026-08-24 (was 'NOT changed, flagged for review'), on Makham's direct instruction that B4 must be 4.10 m. Both B4 verticals now start at dummy row A' (-1.10) instead of row A, span 3.00 -> 4.10 = A'(-1.10) to B(3.00). Confirmed by tracing the beams' OUTER faces, which are uninterrupted by the horizontal beams that frame into the inner faces: grid 2 outer face (x=1384) runs unbroken y=652..1416 px, grid 3 outer face (x=1638) runs y=653..1500 px — both starting at the A' beam's north face (650-655), not at row A (769). Grid 1 (x=1072/1093) and grid 4 (x=1927/1948) by contrast both start at y=758 = row A, so only the two projection verticals extend up to A'. Mark B4 covers A'-to-B and mark B2 covers B-to-C, so the split at row B is a mark change and stays as two entries.

This floor has TWO stairwell-adjacent voids stacked north-south between grid 2 and grid 3: the upper one (rows A'-A'', straddling row A, marked S1 +3.65, flanked by B4) is the stair opening itself (ช่องบันได); the lower one (row B-C, marked S1 +3.75/+3.65) sits directly above it. A third S1 void appears south of row C (grid 2-3) — this is the balcony (ระเบียง +3.65 per architecture หน้า04) rather than a stair-related void.

Row C grid3-4 segment (B1, +3.65) was read by strong pattern consistency with the grid3-4 segment at rows A and B (both confirmed B1 directly) rather than from its own fully legible crop — the specific label at this one segment was partly cut off across zoom crops. Confidence lowered slightly on that element only.

'RB1'(+3.65)' appears once near the lower void's NW corner, same short-beam-stub role as the three RB1' occurrences on หน้า15 — recorded as its own atomic element. UPDATED 2026-08-24: it no longer needs the '~grid2/row B' approximation. This sheet's own left-margin chain prints 1.15 + 1.85 = 3.00 across B-C, and the 1.15 tick (y=1207 px) lands on this stub's south face (beam faces at y=1189-1191 and y=1206-1208) — so it sits on dummy row B'' (pos_m=4.15). grid_ref is now exact ('B''2') and confidence raised 0.5 → 0.75. Named B'' and not B' because หน้า15's 0.55 tick (3.55) was confirmed to carry a beam too and takes the single prime, prime order being top-to-bottom — see the grid master.

The balcony void south of row C (grid2-grid3, B1(+3.65) on all 3 open sides, S1 +3.65) has no column/footing markers at its south corners (plain beam-end crosses only, no 'C1' box) and no printed dimension anywhere in this set gives its south (cantilever) projection length — recorded with approximate grid_ref, same treatment and same reasoning as the ground-floor south recess on หน้า15. This is a real cantilever balcony slab, not a missed dummy-grid case (§4: no dummy grid is invented for a slab/beam edge with no printed length).

This floor's footprint does not reach row D at all (no row-D columns anywhere on this sheet, matching the upper-floor architecture หน้า04 which is smaller than the ground floor) — consistent with the footing plan (หน้า14) also having no D1/D2 footings.
